title: The $9 million bitcoin story is a backtest with the losing branch deleted. -93%, -86%, -84%: could you have held it?
author: QuanTradin
selftext:
The trending story today is that $1,000 of bitcoin in 2011 would be about $9 million now. I keep seeing it framed as a return. It is not a return, it is a backtest with the losing branch deleted, and it is the single best illustration of the thing that breaks most people's strategy testing.

Here is the number nobody puts next to it. Peak to trough, bitcoin fell 93% in 2011, 86% again by 2015, and 84% again by 2018. You did not need to pick the right asset. You needed to sit through being down 93% of your money, three separate times, without selling. Almost nobody does that, which is why almost nobody has the $9 million.

Why this is not just a crypto observation: it is exactly what a bad backtest does to you. It reports the destination and hides the ride. And I got caught by my own version of it last week.

Someone in this sub asked how my equity curve was measured. I gave a confident answer, then went and read my own code. The curve is a running sum over closed trades. So a position that went 40% against me and recovered to a small win draws as a clean step up. The drawdown happened. The stop logic saw it. The picture never did.

My curve was honest about the P&L and dishonest about the ride. Those are different things, and the ride is what makes people quit a strategy that would have worked. It is being rebuilt from per-bar marks, which will make my own results look worse.

Two related things from running the engine on real prices, for whatever they are worth:

Of seven famous strategies I ran through it, five made money and two came back SHELF. The two that failed are ones you can read about in any book. Being widely known did not kill them, they were never as good as the writeups.

And my own live fleet is 888 bots and about 29,500 fills on paper, down heavily. The strategies the engine had already graded negative lost money live too, which is mildly reassuring about the grader and not at all reassuring about me.

Disclosure since my username gives it away: I built the platform. Not selling anything here and not dropping a link. Happy to go into how the per-bar curve is being rebuilt if that is useful to anyone.
